title: TUI selection: the residual not covered by the in-process drive -- bytes to KeyEvent, and model to cells
body:
The TUI's interactive selection IS driven in-process and green. This records the part that is NOT, so the next node does not re-derive it from scratch.

THE BRACKET. The in-process drive runs from `KeyEvent` to the `Screen` MODEL. It does not start at bytes and it does not end at cells.

WHAT IS COVERED TODAY (measured 2026-09-04, `cargo test -p intent-cli --lib`):

- `src/tui/run.rs` tests -- `app.on_key(...)` + `screen_for(...)` + `caret_line(...)` drive the caret key by key in BOTH vocabularies (MENU palette, OMNI omnibox), asserting concrete screen line numbers: arrows, PageUp/PageDown, and the clamp. 16 green.
- `src/tui/app.rs` tests -- the full open/filter/move/commit path including the argv that reaches the realiser, EXHAUSTIVELY over the command vocabulary rather than by sample: `hv_can_open_the_palette_filter_it_and_quit_without_typing_a_colon`, `a_cli_command_and_its_arguments_reach_the_realiser_as_one_argv`, `every_offered_command_is_reachable_by_its_name_and_actually_does_something`, `every_trigger_the_machine_answers_is_acted_on_by_the_realiser`. 52 green.

This is also the harness that now guards the Up/Down inversion hv found (two halves each correct about its own direction, with nothing owning the relation between them).

WHAT IS NOT COVERED -- the residual, and it is two thin things:

(a) crossterm's byte-to-`KeyEvent` decode, plus the `KeyEventKind::Press` filter at `src/tui/run.rs:518`. Nothing drives a real terminal's bytes into the app.
(b) ratatui's render of the `Screen` model to actual cells. Nothing asserts that what the model says reaches the screen.

BOTH ARE THIN AND MOSTLY THIRD-PARTY. What would close them is a smoke test, not a harness: one end-to-end run over a real pty asserting a known frame. Deliberately NOT built -- vc's call 2026-09-04, on the grounds that the cost is real and the residual is bounded.

WHOEVER BUILDS IT WILL HIT PAINT SYNC -- knowing a full-screen frame landed before sending the next key. That is filed separately as a UX item, because the fix that makes it tractable is worth doing on its own terms and must not die with this issue.

THE PRIMITIVES ALREADY EXIST if it is ever wanted, in `native/rust/crates/intent-cli/tests/`: `common::pty_pair` (a real kernel `openpty`, works under CI and any ambient stdin -- `script -q` was tried and fails on a socket stdin), `common::drain`, `organize_default_force_applies.rs` (writes input into the master before spawn), `st_edit_opens_or_prints.rs` (drains the terminal on a concurrent thread while the child runs). Neither call site does both directions at once, and a TUI needs the pty on stdin AND stdout.

PROVENANCE: this issue exists because the work that found it was aimed at the wrong question. The item was held for days on the premise that no harness could drive an interactive selection. Two greps and one `cargo test` refuted that. The gap recorded here is what was ACTUALLY missing, and it is much smaller than the premise assumed.
